_readme: Step 2B benchmark extension. These queries are ADDED to the 21 seed queries in evals/retrieval.json (left untouched). kind: retrieval = at least one real document is relevant; negative = nothing in the corpus is a suitable answer, so an empty result is correct; missing_knowledge = a legitimate question whose answer SHOULD exist but the collection holds no such document (reported as a corpus gap, excluded from quality metrics). expect = relevant document ids (all must be found for full recall). equivalent = interchangeable substitutes, e.g. the same recipe implemented by another renderer. filter = RetrieveFilter passed to the retriever (shot_recipes default to include_draft:true because every recipe is draft today). Every id in expect/equivalent must exist in the corpus; the runner fails otherwise.

queries.query: what is the 180 degree rule
queries.why: Document is titled 'The 180-degree rule'.

queries.query: keeping left and right consistent between two shots of the same action
queries.why: Describes the screen-direction continuity the rule protects, without naming the rule.

queries.query: which goal wins when two editing aims conflict
queries.why: The Murch note ranks cut goals and says to serve the higher one.

queries.query: hide the edit inside a movement so the cut feels smooth
queries.why: Cut-on-motion note: a cut hidden inside a movement feels smoother.

queries.query: keep captions inside the safe area and easy to read
queries.why: Text-legibility note covers line length, hold time and safe area.

queries.query: should two adjacent shots be nearly the same size
queries.why: Note says two adjacent shots of nearly the same size look like a mistake.

queries.query: cut transition shot framing
queries.why: The three notes carrying the cinematography topic; the filter must exclude editing notes such as cut-on-motion.

queries.query: close-up wide shot size variety
queries.why: The only note on shot size (shot-size-progression) is grade B, so min_grade A must leave nothing suitable.

queries.query: problem and solution structure for a short vertical ad
queries.why: Note describes problem, agitate, solution for short vertical ads.

queries.query: ad outline for a food product showcase: attention, interest, desire, action
queries.why: AIDA note suits product showcases such as food.

queries.query: open on the most striking real view of the product instead of a logo
queries.why: Hook note says open on the most striking real view, not a logo.

queries.query: price and health effect statements need approved facts
queries.why: Claims-discipline is the only note tagged claims and covers prices and health effects.

queries.query: pause that marks the end of a chapter
queries.why: dip-to-black is for a chapter break or the end.

queries.query: cut between two scenes that share a shape
queries.why: match-cut is a cut between scenes that share a shape, position or movement.

queries.query: camera drifts toward the subject to build tension
queries.why: slow-push-in is a gradual zoom toward the subject for quiet tension; the HyperFrames variant is the same behaviour.

queries.query: slow zoom in with the HyperFrames renderer
queries.why: The query names the renderer, so only the HyperFrames variant is correct.

queries.query: one large number with a label for a statistic
queries.why: stat-callout shows one large figure with a label.

queries.query: key points that appear one after another as a list
queries.why: bullet-list is a heading with short items that appear in sequence.

queries.query: animated chart and product interface demo with a cursor
queries.why: scene-composition draws UI demos with a cursor and illustrative charts.

queries.query: name tag that slides in near the bottom of the frame
queries.why: lower-third-slide slides a name or label in near the bottom.

queries.query: play the supplied footage with text over it
queries.why: clip-play-caption plays the clip with the overlay text as a caption.

queries.query: tight crop on the label texture of the product
queries.why: crop-to-detail reframes to a detail such as texture or a label.

queries.query: energetic reveal of the new feature with impact
queries.why: Both are high-energy: punch-in lands on a key feature, the wipe suits product reveals.

queries.query: calm closing scene where the logo appears and viewers read the call to action
queries.why: End card holds the call to action; logo-reveal shows the brand mark at sign off.

queries.query: energetic change between scenes
queries.why: directional-wipe is the only high-energy transition.

queries.query: zoom
queries.why: At a 1.0s scene only punch-in-emphasis (min 0.8s) is allowed; the other camera moves need at least 1.5s.

queries.query: big figure result
queries.why: stat-callout is the graphics-only recipe for a figure; media [] keeps graphics-only scenes.

queries.query: slow zoom in
queries.why: No recipe doc carries recipe_implemented in this corpus, so implemented_only must return nothing.

queries.query: slow zoom in
queries.why: Production default: every recipe is draft, so nothing is retrievable without include_draft.

queries.query: safe area for captions on TikTok
queries.why: platform_specs holds only a README; no verified spec exists.

queries.query: maximum video length for Instagram Reels
queries.why: No verified platform spec exists.

queries.query: loudness target for YouTube Shorts
queries.why: No verified platform spec exists; audio-ducking-loudness in directing_principles only covers EBU R 128 broadcast.

queries.query: does the product contain added sugar
queries.why: Brand facts are created per project at runtime; the corpus holds none.

queries.query: brand colours and logo usage rules
queries.why: No brand facts exist in the corpus.

queries.query: approved storyboard for a coffee reel
queries.why: approved_examples has no documents.

queries.query: previously approved ad that performed well
queries.why: approved_examples has no documents.

queries.query: how to color grade footage with LUTs
queries.why: No note covers color grading; 'footage' appears in other notes, so BM25 may still return noise.

queries.query: quarterly tax filing deadlines
queries.why: Entirely out of domain.

queries.query: render a photorealistic video of a dragon
queries.why: No recipe generates new footage (reframing-limits: 'We do not shoot new footage'); 'video' appears in many recipes.

queries.query: quantum computing hardware benchmarks
queries.why: Entirely out of domain.

queries.query: avoid pixelation when enlarging low-resolution clips
queries.why: Reframing-limits explains that every zoom crops the source and costs resolution; the query uses different terms (pixelation, enlarging).

queries.query: dolly in on the bottle
queries.why: A dolly-in is a gradual move toward the subject; slow-push-in is the matching recipe but never uses the word dolly.

queries.query: voiceover must stay audible over the background track
queries.why: music-bed-duck lowers music under speech; the query uses different terms (voiceover, background track).
